text.p: The retention of long-term take-or-pay contracts is vital to the development of the gas industry, Nazim Zouioueche, director general of Algerian state oil and gas company Sonatrach, said on Thursday.
Speaking at the Gas Executives Summit conference, Zouioueche predicted that European gas demand was set to grow to 450 billion cubic metres (bcm) a year by 2010.
This would put pressure on producers such as Algeria, Russia and Norway to fill the supply gap.
But he said liberalisation of markets under way in Europe, particularly in Britain, jeopardised producers' plans.
"Gas producers are attentive to changes in consumer markets," he said.
"Changes downsteam are not helpful to the capital instensive upstream.

"The retention of long-term contracts is vital for the industry. Development of gas is not possible if we are not sure what we will be paid. The development of gas in a slump raises real problems in such a particularly capital-intensive business.
"We are watching the wave of deregulation. The British experiment and the development of the IPE (International Petroleum Exchange) contract will be determining factors here," Zouioueche said.
Long-term take-or-pay contracts have been mired in controversy since market liberalisation began in Britain.

Monopoly buyer British Gas Plc found itself paying for large volumes of gas at fixed prices while the spot price fell following the introduction of deregulation, and both consumers and producers have watched developments closely.
Zouioueche said European gas demand was growing, but development was hampered by by the fuel's price leakage to oil, as he believed oil prices are too low.
"We meed a price readjustment," he said.

He added that natural gas accounted for 63 percent of Sonatrach's hydrocarbon reserves and that the company was looking to raise exports to 60 billion cubic metres a year through pipleines and by shipping liquefied natural gas (LNG).
